page.layout: One page of text in a single column; margin notes in the left margin (Ouid. lib. I. Metam.; Lucan. lib. I.; Ortus, Occasus, Meridies, Septentrio; Dionysius; Libya, seu Africa; Europa; Asia). Running head at top; page number 4 at top left. Ornamental strapwork band below the opening verse, then a heading, then running text, a centred line, more text, and a closing parenthetical at the foot.

p.i: At tibi, quacunque es Libyco gens igne dirempta, In Noton umbra cadit, qua nobis exit in Arcton. Te segnis Cynosura subit: tu sicca profundo Mergi plaustra putas: nullumque in vertice summo Sidus habes immune maris, procul axis utrumque est, Et fuga signorum medio rapit omnia coelo.

main_text.head: TERRÆ DIVISIO IN QVATUOR regiones, Orientem, Occidentem, Meridiem, Septentrionem.

p.i: E Vrus ad Auroram, Nabathæaque regna recessit, Persidaque, & radiis iuga subdita matutinis. Vesper, & occiduo qua littora sole tepescunt, Proxima sunt Zephyro: Scythiam septemque triones Horrifer inuasit Boreas: contraria tellus Nubibus assiduis, pluuioque madescit ab Austro. Vnde venit Titan, & nox vbi sidera condit: Quaque dies medius flagrantibus æstuat horis: Et qua bruma rigens, ac nescia vere remitti Astringit Scythicum glacialí frigore Pontum.

main_text.p: Ouid. lib. I. Metam.Terræ diuisio in tres præcipuas partes, Europam, Africam, & Asiam.

p.i: Homines Terram tres in continentes partiti sunt: Primùm quidem Libyam, deinde verò Europam, Asiámque. Sed certè Libya quidem ab Europa habet terminum Obliquum in lineis, Grades, & os[ostia] Nili: Vbi maximè Borealis est recessus Ægypti, Et fanum percelebre Amyclæi Canopi. Europam autem ab Asia Tanais in medio disterminat:

page.notes: Marginal notes at left are keyed by position; the Dionysius, Libya seu Africa, Europa and Asia labels are small marginal words. Page is a scan with show-through and stains; the first verse lines and the closing parenthesis "(Quu" at the foot are partly damaged and read with uncertainty; "(Qua" is read as printed. Bracketed "[ostia]" appears in the original text. Greek and ornamental elements not transcribed beyond the band.
